name: Cavernous sinus
summary: A plexus of venous channels within the dura on each side of the sella and sphenoid body, more important for what passes through it than for the blood it drains. The internal carotid artery and the abducens nerve run inside it; the oculomotor, trochlear, ophthalmic and maxillary nerves lie in its lateral wall. It receives the ophthalmic veins from the orbit and the sphenoparietal sinus and drains to the petrosal sinuses, and the two sides communicate around the pituitary. Its lesions, whether thrombosis from facial infection, a carotid-cavernous fistula, a pituitary tumor or a meningioma, all produce the cavernous sinus syndrome of ophthalmoplegia, facial numbness in V1/V2, proptosis and chemosis, with a Horner syndrome from the carotid sympathetic plexus.

anatomy.location: Lateral to the sella turcica and sphenoid body from the superior orbital fissure to the petrous apex, medial to the temporal lobe and uncus; roofed by dura carrying the anterior clinoid process and bounded medially by the pituitary and sphenoid sinus.

subdivisions.name: Contents (within the sinus)
subdivisions.note: internal carotid artery (cavernous segment) with its sympathetic plexus, abducens nerve

subdivisions.name: Lateral wall (from above down)
subdivisions.note: oculomotor nerve, trochlear nerve, ophthalmic nerve V1, maxillary nerve V2

subdivisions.name: Tributaries
subdivisions.note: superior and inferior ophthalmic veins, sphenoparietal sinus, superficial middle cerebral vein

subdivisions.name: Drainage
subdivisions.note: superior and inferior petrosal sinuses, intercavernous sinuses, emissary veins to the pterygoid plexus

function: Venous drainage of the orbit and anterior cranial base; conduit for the internal carotid artery and the nerves of eye movement and facial sensation.

arteries: (venous structure) drains territories of the cerebral arteries

bestView.label: cavernous sinuses either side of the pituitary with the carotid flow voids inside
cavernous sinus lateral to the sella from the orbital fissure to the petrous apex

imaging.normalAppearance: On coronal T1+Gd the sinus enhances homogeneously around the dark carotid flow void, with a flat or concave lateral wall; a convex, bulging, asymmetric or non-enhancing sinus is abnormal. Cranial nerves III, IV, V1 and V2 are seen as dots in the lateral wall on high-resolution T2.

pathology.finding: Expanded sinus with filling defects on contrast, engorged superior ophthalmic vein, proptosis, usually from facial or sphenoid infection.
Enlarged sinus and superior ophthalmic vein with arterialized flow; DSA confirms.

pathology.pathology: Cavernous sinus meningioma or pituitary adenoma extension
pathology.finding: Enhancing tissue encasing the carotid with a convex lateral wall.
Enhancing inflammatory tissue in the sinus and orbital apex responding to steroids.

imaging.sequenceOfChoice: Coronal T1+Gd and thin T2 through the sella; CT/MR venography; DSA for fistula

lesionEffects.deficit: Ophthalmoplegia of III, IV and VI, sometimes complete
lesionEffects.mechanism: Nerves in and beside the sinus

lesionEffects.deficit: Numbness of the forehead and cheek (V1, V2), sparing the jaw (V3)
lesionEffects.mechanism: Lateral wall nerves; V3 leaves through the foramen ovale below the sinus

lesionEffects.deficit: Horner syndrome with a sixth nerve palsy
lesionEffects.mechanism: Sympathetic plexus on the cavernous carotid next to the abducens nerve

examination: Eye movements in all directions, ptosis, pupil
Corneal reflex and sensation in V1, V2 and V3
Proptosis, conjunctival injection, listen for an orbital bruit
pearls: Multiple ocular motor palsies with V1/V2 numbness on one side is the cavernous sinus or superior orbital fissure; add optic nerve involvement and it is the orbital apex
Horner syndrome plus abducens palsy is almost pathognomonic of a cavernous sinus lesion
